newsitem.title: USA: Cablevision, ITT tussle over MSG. [CORRECTED 16:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Cablevision, ITT tussle over MSG. [CORRECTED 16:00 GMT]

text.p: A two-year-old partnership between Cablevision Systems Corp and ITT Corp is being rattled by a dispute about ownership rights to Madison Square Garden.
ITT is widely expected to sell its 50 percent stake in the Madison Square Garden properties as part of an attempt to fend off a $6.5 billion hostile takeover from Hilton Hotels Corp.
The New York-based company rejected the Hilton offer last week and said it would consider selling non-core assets in order to focus on its Sheraton hotels and Caesars casino business.

Cablevision chairman Charles Dolan (corrects from "chief executive officer James Dolan") said on Tuesday that he would be interested in buying the rest of Madison Square Garden that his firm does not already own. Dolan also contends that Cablevision has first right of refusal for ITT's 50 percent stake.
"We definitely have first right of refusal and they have acknowledged that," he said of ITT.

But ITT spokesman Jim Gallagher on Tuesday disputed that claim, saying the partnership pact between the two companies does not grant Cablevision first crack at the properties, which include the world-famous arena, the Knicks professional basketball team and the MSG network.
Cablevision and ITT teamed up in 1995 to buy the Garden properties.

Gallagher declined to comment on whether ITT was holding talks with other prospective bidders. However, Wall Street experts have speculated that several companies would likely seek to buy the Madison Square Garden properties.
Meanwhile, a controversy arose on Tuesday when Cablevision said it paid to ITT the balance of funds needed to boost its Madison Square Garden stake to 50 percent from 26.6 percent.

ITT quickly objected to Cablevision's cash payment of $168.75 million plus interest, saying that it previously had notified Cablevision that it would exercise its right to take a portion of the balance in ownership of SportsChannel.
Cablevision owns SportsChannel, which has television rights to many of New York's professional sports teams.
"ITT unilaterally retains its right to take 50 percent ownership of Cablevision's SportsChannel...," ITT said in a news release.
In a telephone interview, Dolan said Cablevision would be willing to hand over the SportsChannel stake as soon as previously-set conditions were met.

"At the point that those conditions have been satisfied, then if they want SportsChannel, they can have SportsChannel. They can have that 50 percent simply by repaying to us the 50 percent of what we paid them today," he said.
Dolan also said Cablevision's relationship with ITT remained solid.

"I think we're both doing what we need to do for the benefit of our shareholders and that might seem to have posed a conflict. Our relationship has been excellent for more than two years. We have worked in a very effective partnership in managing the Garden and if they decide not to sell, that's the way it will continue," he said.
